subject: extraconstr and observation matrices with rgeneric

messages.author: b91e54f3020c0cfd
messages.subject: extraconstr and observation matrices with rgeneric
parts:
Dear INLA experts

Before starting to implement codes that would not work, I prefer to ask here...

I would like to use the rgeneric framework to implement very specific restrictions on latent space-time models (SPDE+AR1), such as condition one location at the first observation time to be 0.

Is it possible to use the observation matrix mechanism from the SPDE implementations for rgeneric-effects?
Is it possible to impose conditions on the variables in a rgeneric model  using the extraconstr-mechanism?

Thanks for help.

Thomas

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] extraconstr and observation matrices with rgeneric
parts:
I'm not sure I get this right, but for a rgeneric model, x, you want to
condition on that x[1] = 0 ?

In that case, then can you do the conditioning yourself within the
rgeneric, as the prec matrix would be Q[2:n,2:n].

using constraints, saying that x[1] = 0, will make the posterior for
that node singular, a point mass at 0, which is not supported.

In case you fit the model, and then want to do the conditioning, its
possible to use inla.posterior.sample() for this, see the vignette

Conditional sampling from a fitted model - PDF source R code

in the package.

An alternative, is to condition on x[1]=0, almost, by forcing that one
to be close to 0, by introducting an 'observation' this is so, like a
Normal with mean x[1] and high fixed precision.

there is some issues about the normalizing constant for the conditional
distribution (on x[1]=0) being informative about some hyperparameters,
but this depends on which of the approaches above that is being used,
and also, if you see this as fitting a conditional model, compared to
doing conditioning in a fitted model.

Best
H

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] extraconstr and observation matrices with rgeneric
parts:
Hi Thomas,

The case of constraining on individual nodes in SPDE models is best done by using the remaining sub graph Q, as discussed. It’s a special case of a restriction of the degrees of freedom of the basis function space, that I partly implemented for 1D mesh/sde models, where one can set the boundary to be Dirichlet or Neumann, or free, which corresponds to keeping and/or modifying the boundary basis functions, and works both for degree 1 and degree 2 b-splines. If there is broad usefulness of such a feature I can consider implementing that for 2d meshes in the future standalone fmesher package, which will likely handle things a bit more like PDE solver packages that define the function space that the solutions live on. That could then perhaps make such rgeneric models easier to implement.

Finn

Hi Finn

thanks for these explanations, and great that there will be a separate fmesher package!

Currently, we are using this conditioning approach for models for conditional extremes where we have Gaussian components that are conditioned on the value at a single space-time observation point. I don't know about other important applications, but having this conditioning feature in the future fmesher package would of course be great!

Thomas
